extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of historical arithmetic and elementary number theory (Italian-language mathematical treatise readers)
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a historical Italian arithmetic/number theory treatise describing definitions, classifications, and properties of numbers (parity, multiples, parts/aliquots, prime/composite, figurate numbers, powers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of binary powers / positional generation (1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeatedly multiplying the unit by two (lo:2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, ...) produces a continuing sequence; these are discussed as binary/quaternary positions and as fundamental termini (extremes, medii, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and repeated examples are given: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 ...; how taking 'any' term and multiplying/dividing by 2 moves you along the sequence; discussions of middle and extreme terms and how multiplication of extremes/middles yields other members (e.g., multiply middle term and extremes to obtain other powers). Several examples illustrate the positional relations (e.g., '1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128').

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity classification and behavior under operations (even/odd rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and properties of even (pari) and odd (impari) numbers, including how parity behaves under multiplication and addition, and the formation of paired sequences of even/odd terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text repeatedly examines how multiplying by 2, 3, etc. affects parity, how terms that are 'parimente pari' arise, and gives procedural examples of generating sequences of even and odd numbers by multiplication (e.g., demonstrating which positions become even or odd when multiplied by given factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of equal parts (division into partes, aliquota)
rubrics_metrics.description: How a number (or the unit) may be divided into equal parts (parti uguali / aliquote), naming of parts (prima, seconda, terza parte) and conditions for when such divisions are possible or impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of dividing a unit into halves, quarters, thirds, etc.; discussion of when a part is 'aliquota' (exact divisor) versus 'non aliquota' (not an exact divisor) and implications for measuring and enumerating the whole from its parts. Gives numeric illustrations (e.g., halves, thirds, fourths, ninths) and rules about when a part can or cannot exactly measure the unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aliquot (aliquota) vs non-aliquot parts and measurability
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for a part to be aliquot (i.e., an exact part of a number) and consequences when a part is not aliquot — inability to 'measure' or enumerate the whole integrally by that part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that if a part is not aliquot then it cannot measure the whole integrally (non-measurable), with examples and the notion that some parts are 'non aliquota' and therefore non-enumerable as whole units; references to specific cases where a part cannot be multiplied to yield the unit exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primality and compositeness (numero primo e composito / incomposti e composti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of numbers into prime (incomposti) and composite (composti): primes cannot be formed by multiplying smaller integral parts, while composites can be expressed as a product of other numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and examples: description of the property that primes have no integral divisors apart from unit and themselves; composites decompose into factors. The text uses the taxonomy 'primo' and 'compofito/composito' and presents examples and formation rules, including how composite numbers arise from multiplying units/other numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation / origin of numbers by multiplication (creazione / generazione)
rubrics_metrics.description: How numbers are 'created' or generated by multiplication from the unit and from previously generated numbers; includes the idea of 'mother' unit and offspring numbers produced by successive multiplications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise uses metaphors ('madre vnita', 'regina') and traces generation paths (e.g., multiply the mother unit by various factors to obtain offspring numbers), providing sequences and examples of how families of numbers originate from a base unit (including repeated multiplications and formation of species).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy of number species and denominations (first, second, third species etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic naming/denoting of parts and species of numbers (prima, seconda, terza specie, etc.) according to their relation to the unit and to each other when numbers are partitioned or compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text enumerates species and assigns names based on which part of the whole they are (e.g., 'la nona parte', 'la terza parte'), showing how those denominations are used to characterize numbers and their relationships; includes examples where particular parts are named and how that naming informs arithmetic operations and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figurate numbers and geometric analogy (triangular, square, pentagonal, hexagonal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of numbers corresponding to geometric figures (triangulare, quadrato, pentagono, esagono) and the relation between arithmetic sequences and polygonal/figurate constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that numbers can be represented by geometric figures (triangular numbers, square numbers, etc.) and discusses how adding units or other numbers corresponds to enlarging these figures; gives examples mapping sets of numbers to triangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons and relates this to arithmetic operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity (similitudine) of numbers and behavior of products
rubrics_metrics.description: Concept of numbers being 'simili' (similar/sufficiently alike) — when numbers share certain proportional or structural properties — and how their products (especially squares) preserve/reflect these similarities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses that similar numbers when multiplied produce related (e.g., square) numbers; shows examples where multiplying 'similar' numbers yields a square and examines necessary accompanying factors (e.g., when supplementary factors are required to produce a square). Mentions ratios of 'latitudine' and 'longitudine' metaphorically to explain proportional similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for forming new species by composition and repeated multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: How new number species arise by composing (componere) numbers together and by repeated multiplication of certain bases, with rules governing when such composition yields numbers of a given species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains processes of composing numbers (composito/compofito) and how repeated multiplication (including by powers) can create families (species) of numbers, gives examples of comparing composed numbers to other numbers and how composed parts are denoted and classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of middle and extreme terms in sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes relations among 'medio' (middle) and 'estremo' (extreme) terms in sequences formed by multiplications (e.g., how extremes and middles multiply to give other canonical members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples indicate multiplying an extreme by a corresponding middle term yields a larger term in the same progression (e.g., operations among entries in 1,2,4,8,... ). The treatise repeatedly returns to the concept of middle/extreme positions and how shifting or multiplying them changes the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and practical enumeration procedures (examples of counting/multiplying to enumerate numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural examples for enumerating, multiplying and comparing numbers; specific numeric sequences used to illustrate counting and measurement operations (including composite processes like 'multiply then add' to reach particular totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many step-by-step numeric illustrations are included (e.g., 'se tu multiplicarbi 3 via 4 fa 12', 'multiplica 3 via 16 fa 48', sequences like 1,2,4,... used to show operations). The author demonstrates practical enumeration and measurement techniques using these worked numeric examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of impossibility conditions (when divisions or equal parts cannot be formed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and examples showing when a given division or equality cannot be achieved integrally (e.g., when a part is non-aliquot or a proposed denomination cannot exist within the unit), and the consequences of such impossibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise explains circumstances where one cannot form an integral part (e.g., cannot divide the unit into that many equal integral parts), and uses examples (specific denominators and failures) to illustrate non-measurability and the resulting restrictions on naming or composing numbers.
